case_name: Smt. Sunita And Another ... vs State Of Uttarakhand

parties.respondent_defendant: State of Uttarakhand (Respondent No.2) and Sunil Kumar (Respondent No.1)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Smt. Sunita and another got married in 1999 and had a daughter. The parties have been involved in various allegations and counter-allegations. The revisionist initiated proceedings under the Hindu Marriage Act, which was filed before the Family Court. The case was taken ex parte and the marriage was dissolved.

legal_principles.principle: The effect of an interim order can be that an order of restraint is kept in abeyance.
legal_principles.held: the judicial effect of it would be that an order of restraint from solemnizing the second marriage, that was kept in abeyance, meaning thereby, the embargo for the respondent to solemnize the second marriage that was eradicated by the interim order dated 11th January, 2008.

legal_principles.principle: A person who has attained the age of majority cannot be granted maintenance under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: since she has attained the age of majority, she could not be granted maintenance under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C.

outcome.final_order: The parties were present in person and made an effort to resolve the controversy. The Court considered the backdrop of the case before making a decision.

keywords: Protection of Women from DV Act
